text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — ran into a pretty sneaky bug with the Python SDK observability middleware + FastAPI. Request ID header gets set, but inside async background tasks / create_task the request id becomes None. Repro below.

Noah Patel: ugh, can you paste a minimal repro? which SDK version?

Maria Chen: using redwood-sdk==0.9.2. Minimal:
```py
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks, Request
from redwood_sdk.observability import ObservabilityMiddleware, set_request_id_from_headers
app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(ObservabilityMiddleware)

@app.post('/work')
async def work(req: Request, bg: BackgroundTasks):
    set_request_id_from_headers(req.headers)
    def bg_job(rid):
        # prints None instead of the request id
        print('bg job rid=', rid)
    bg.add_task(bg_job, getattr(req.state, 'request_id', None))
    return {'ok': True}
```
Run with uvicorn app:app --reload, then curl -H 'X-Request-ID: abc-123' -X POST localhost:8000/work

Susan Li: This rings a bell — contextvars don't automatically propagate into create_task/background tasks in some runtimes. You need to propagate context explicitly or use contextvars.copy_context().

Ryan Morgan: Thanks for the repro Maria. We were seeing something similar in internal traces. The middleware sets request id on a contextvar, but we don't wrap task creation. Can you confirm if you also hit this when using HTTPX async clients inside the request scope?

Maria Chen: Yep, same behavior when I do `asyncio.create_task(some_coro())` inside handler. The HTTPX client call in the handler has the right request id, but inside the background task it's None.

Jon Kline: Feature request: can we add an official helper to auto-instrument asyncio task creation? e.g., `from redwood_sdk.observability import instrument_asyncio_tasks()` that patches `asyncio.create_task` to copy context. Also: typed protocol for the hook callback would help editors.

Noah Patel: +1 for a FastAPI sample app in the SDK examples. I keep copy-pasting the same wrapper.

Ryan Morgan: We're tracking this. There's an open PR that adds an AsyncTask wrapper and updates the ObservabilityMiddleware to offer two options: "auto-propagate-tasks" (opt-in) and a manual `bind_context()` util. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/418 (ci pending). Can you test the branch?

Maria Chen: tried the branch — helps for `create_task` but my FastAPI BackgroundTasks still fails (since it uses an internal threadpool). stacktrace: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'` when reading request id in the thread.

Susan Li: BackgroundTasks uses starlette's threadpool executor which doesn't pick contextvars either. For thread pools you either pass the value explicitly or use a contextvar-to-thread bridge. Workaround: capture `rid = get_request_id()` then pass as arg to background fn.

Ryan Morgan: Agreed. Long-term we should document both approaches and provide a `copy_context_to_thread(fn)` helper. I'll update the PR to include docs + typed signatures for the middleware hooks (Jon's request).

Jon Kline: For typing, suggest API like: `MiddlewareHook = Callable[[Mapping[str,str], ContextVars], Awaitable[None]]` — but we should keep it simple (Mapping[str,str] for headers, str for request_id).

Maria Chen: Another DX thing — the observability docs only show otel export in JS. Can we add an OpenTelemetry example for Python with tracerprovider + span exporter + automatic context propagation? That would have saved me an hour.

Ryan Morgan: Good point. I'll add a FastAPI + OTEL quickstart in the repo examples and a sample app under examples/fastapi-observability. Also adding a small section on "request id propagation patterns" (in-request, pass-arg, instrument-asyncio, thread bridge).

ci-bot: build #418 — tests failing on windows matrix (flaky).

Noah Patel: thanks all — will try the branch once CI stabilizes. If anyone needs a mini-repro app I can paste mine into examples too. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: thanks! appreciate the quick turn. :eyes:
